questions.q: How does Snowflake separate storage cost from compute cost?
options: Compute cost includes storage cost automatically at no extra charge
They are billed completely independently — storage is a flat per-TB/month rate, compute is credits consumed by whichever warehouse runs a query
Storage is free as long as you have an active warehouse
Storage and compute are always billed together as one combined line item
questions.explain: Snowflake's architecture separates storage and compute, and its billing follows the same split — a warehouse that never runs a query costs nothing in compute, no matter how much data sits in storage.

questions.q: A Medium (M) warehouse runs for 1 hour. A Small (S) warehouse runs for 2 hours. How do the credits compare?
options: They cost the same number of credits
The Small costs more because it ran longer
Credits aren't affected by warehouse size, only by query count
The Medium costs four times as many credits
questions.explain: Each size doubles the credit-per-hour rate of the size below it (S=2/hr, M=4/hr), so 1 hour of Medium (4 credits) equals 2 hours of Small (2+2=4 credits).

questions.q: How are Snowflake credits actually metered?
options: Per day, based on a daily flat fee
Per second, with a 60-second minimum each time a warehouse resumes from suspension
Per hour only, rounded up to the nearest hour
Per query, regardless of how long the query runs
questions.explain: Credits are metered per second, not per query or per hour, with the one exception being a 60-second minimum billed whenever a suspended warehouse resumes.

questions.q: Which account_usage view logs actual credit consumption per warehouse?
options: LOGIN_HISTORY
TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS
QUERY_HISTORY
WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY
questions.explain: ACCOUNT_USAGE.WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY logs the credits each warehouse actually consumed, which is what the real Snowsight screenshot in this lesson queries.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does querying real credit consumption by warehouse usually reveal?
options: Storage cost always exceeds compute cost in every account
Credit usage is impossible to see without contacting Snowflake support
A handful of warehouses account for most of the credits, while several sit provisioned but nearly unused
Every warehouse in an account always consumes an identical number of credits
questions.explain: The real screenshot in this lesson shows exactly this pattern — a few warehouses dominate credit consumption while others sit near zero, which is the most common real-world cost story.
